name: linear-customer-to-notion-company

deploy.description: When a customer is created in Linear, match it to a Notion Companies record by domain (creating the company if there is none) and write the Linear customer id onto that page. Source of truth: https://github.com/work-flowers/zapier-sdk/tree/main/linear-customer-to-notion-company
deploy.enable_on_publish_note: Parked at first publish so it could not double-write alongside the then-live classic Zap. Cutover done 2026-08-22; kept as the record of why v1 shipped disabled. A republish carries the CURRENT enabled state forward (read off Zapier), so this no longer affects anything.

trigger.trigger_note: Linear INSTANT trigger on new customers, same as the classic Zap. `list-trigger-input-fields` reports no input fields, so params is empty. Zapier registers the Linear-side subscription itself — there is no external URL to hand out or repoint.

connections_note: Only Notion is used by a step. The Linear connection is bound to the TRIGGER (trigger.authentication_id): the workflow reads the customer off the trigger payload and never calls back into Linear.

notion.note: Match property: 'Website' (url). Write-back property: 'Linear Customer ID' (rich_text). Notion's url filter has no host-aware operator, so the `contains` query is a coarse prefilter and the hostname comparison is redone exactly in code — 'acme.com' must not match 'notacme.com'. Creation goes through NotionCLIAPI write create_database_item with template_mode 'default' (repo rule 5), falling back to a plain create when the data source has no default template.

tables.01JM8PH8YM93A482M8BFZ6WKW6: [Table] Company IDs — NOT written by this workflow. The classic Zap wrote f7/f5/f9/f11 directly; the durable writes the Linear customer id to the Notion page and lets notion-companies-to-zapier-table mirror it into the Table, the same division of labour as notion-company-to-linear-customer.

replaces_classic_zap: Update New Linear Customer in Zapier Table

cutover.classic_zap_disabled: 2026-08-22 — confirmed by Dennis. Not machine-verifiable: classic Zaps are exposed by neither the SDK CLI nor the MCP connector.
cutover.status: complete — this durable is the only thing resolving new Linear customers to Notion Companies. The duplicate-company risk from an overlap is now moot.

behaviour_changes: BUG FIX: the classic Zap's fallback path wrote {{1__domains}} into f7 'Linear Customer ID', so existing rows carry hostnames (e.g. tanninroad.com.au) where a Linear customer UUID belongs — the same defect already noted in notion-company-to-linear-customer's zap.json. The durable writes the real customer id. Existing bad values are left as they are; they are corrected the next time that customer fires.

The Table is no longer written directly. Writing the id to the Notion page and letting notion-companies-to-zapier-table mirror it keeps one owner for the mirror instead of two writers racing on the same row.
Domain matching is now exact on the hostname. The classic Zap used an `icontains` filter on f9 Domain, so a customer at 'acme.com' could match a stored 'notacme.com'.

A customer with no domain, and a domainless customer with no name, now skip with a reason instead of creating a Notion company with a blank Website that the next domainless customer would collide with.

The write is guarded on the id already present, so the echo of notion-company-to-linear-customer (which creates Linear customers FROM Notion companies and writes the id back) converges instead of the two workflows writing at each other.

related.notion-company-to-linear-customer: The opposite direction: Notion company linked to a deal -> create the Linear customer, write the id back to the page. Together the two form a loop that terminates on the 'already-linked' guard in this workflow.

description: Linear instant trigger (new customer) -> find or create the matching Notion Companies record by domain and write the Linear customer id onto it; the Companies mirror carries it into [Table] Company IDs.
